title: Jonah Flees and Is Swallowed
summary: The LORD tells Jonah to go to Nineveh and cry against its wickedness, but Jonah goes to Joppa and boards a ship for Tarshish. A great storm arises, and the frightened sailors cast lots, and the lot falls on Jonah, who says he fears the LORD, the God of heaven, and tells them to throw him overboard. They try to row to land, then do so, and the sea calms. A great fish swallows Jonah, and for three days and nights he prays from its belly; the fish vomits him onto dry land.

title: Nineveh Repents
summary: The LORD again tells Jonah to go to Nineveh, and he goes and cries that in forty days it will be overthrown. The people of Nineveh believe God and proclaim a fast, and all, great and small, put on sackcloth. The king leaves his throne, covers himself with sackcloth and sits in ashes, and decrees that people and animals fast and turn from violence, saying, 'Who can tell if God will turn and repent?' God sees their works and relents from the disaster he had said he would do.

title: Jonah's Anger
summary: Jonah is very displeased and angry, and prays that he knew God was gracious and merciful, which is why he fled to Tarshish; he asks to die. The LORD asks if he does well to be angry. Jonah camps east of the city, and God makes a gourd grow up to shade him. At dawn God prepares a worm that kills the gourd, and a hot east wind and sun leave Jonah faint. God says Nineveh has more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and much cattle. The book ends on this question.
